name: mixed-roles
why: same-role runs fold without a new "Role:" prefix; alternating roles start a new line; a tool entry resets the role so the next same-role chunk re-prefixes. This is the core rendering contract §2.7 must not change for the default text digest.

name: tool-calls
why: exercises every tool branch: title/kind fallbacks, whitespace collapse, rawOutput fallback, empty output, the 400-char per-result cap, non-terminal updates ignored, and non-text content contributing nothing.

name: no-digestible-content
why: events that produce no digest text (thought chunks, plan, non-text message content, a pending tool update) must still advance throughSeq while leaving text empty — catches a regression that either emits stray text or loses the seq watermark.

name: empty
why: zero events: empty text, throughSeq 0, no truncation marker. The degenerate input a bounding rewrite is most likely to break.

name: oversized-tail-truncation
why: exceeds an explicit small maxChars so the current tail-biased policy is frozen: oldest content dropped, truncation marker prepended, TAIL-MARKER surviving and HEAD-MARKER gone. This is the exact behaviour §2.7 adds head/head-tail options beside — the default must not drift.

name: oversized-default-budget
why: crosses the 32 000-char DEFAULT bound with no opts — the configuration the resume chain actually uses, so a change to the default budget or policy is caught even if explicit-maxChars behaviour is preserved.

name: utf8-multibyte-truncation
why: CJK, astral-plane emoji (surrogate pairs), a flag sequence, a skin-tone modifier and a combining accent, forced past the budget so the slice lands inside multi-byte text. §2.7 moves bounding from JS chars to UTF-8 bytes; this fixture makes any change to where the cut falls visible instead of silent.

name: utf8-split-surrogate
why: the same corpus at a budget whose cut falls inside a surrogate pair: the current char-based slice emits a lone low surrogate (half of a flag emoji). Captured as it is today, NOT as an expectation — AC-7.2 requires truncation to back up to a valid UTF-8 boundary, so this golden is the before-picture of a defect §2.7 is expected to fix, and a diff here needs a human ruling, not an auto-refresh.

name: boundary-exact-fit
why: text length lands exactly on maxChars: the current bound is inclusive, so no truncation and no marker. An off-by-one in a rewritten bounder shows up here and nowhere else.

name: boundary-one-over
why: one char past maxChars — the smallest input that must truncate. Pins the exact trigger point together with boundary-exact-fit.

name: boundary-budget-below-marker
why: maxChars smaller than the truncation marker itself: the degenerate case where no content can survive. Frozen so a rewrite cannot start emitting a marker that overflows its own budget.
